### Log request: histor.modelmarket.dev/log (staging, 10qps list)

## Александр Артамохов

30 Oct '26

10:51 a.m.

Hello, I would like to request that HISTOR's log be added to the staging witness network, on the 10qps list. vkey histor.modelmarket.dev/log+ad3ca066+AfXpkWqXVW93sChXnhKsNzvGLTFAAredl1jLlEjbr4wU qpd 144 contact alexar76@rambler.ru Origin line: histor.modelmarket.dev/log (equal to the vkey key name). Key type 0x01, Ed25519. Checkpoint: https://histor.modelmarket.dev/checkpoint https://histor.modelmarket.dev/checkpoint Add-checkpoint rate: one request per witness every 10 minutes (144 per day), from a timer on the log's host. The log only grows; consistency proofs are served at https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/log/proof/consistency?first=&second= https://histor.modelmarket.dev/api/v1/log/proof/consistency?first=&second= and the witness client handles 409 by resubmitting from the witness's size. What it is: HISTOR is a public, append-only log of the tool definitions that MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers listed in the official MCP registry actually serve. Each observation becomes a signed statement, and the statements are leaves of an RFC 9162 Merkle tree (currently about 1.29 million leaves, growing by a few thousand a day). The format is specified at https://github.com/alexar76/histor/blob/main/docs/spec/transparency-log.md https://github.com/alexar76/histor/blob/main/docs/spec/transparency-log.md with test vectors; the checkpoint and note formats were checked byte for byte against golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/note and github.com/transparency-dev/formats/note. Intended users: MCP clients and security tooling that want to check whether the tool definitions they received are the ones the server serves to everyone (split-view detection for tool definitions), and researchers using the weekly open dataset (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23512759). Witness cosignatures are what would turn the log's own signed heads into evidence that it shows everyone the same tree. Load versus utility: 144 add-checkpoint requests per witness per day, small checkpoints, no burst. Expected lifetime: long-lived; the log has run since September 2026 and the origin and key will not change. The same instance also implements c2sp.org/tlog-witness https://histor.modelmarket.dev/witness/v1, https://histor.modelmarket.dev/witness/v1, key histor.modelmarket.dev/witness+87df9f83+BHmgo3SRWlaehFMgWBDIOWFgs1V2YQS+ufBcg/ht6kw/). It is not offered as a network witness yet; if that would be useful once it has run for a while, I would be glad to discuss it separately. Thank you, Aleksandr Artamokhov--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Yellow, White and Green

Orienteering maps show different types of vegetation (trees and bushes) with colour.

Yellow is used to indicate clear areas and green is used to show dense vegetation, with darker shades for denser vegetation.

White on the map is forest cover with ample space between trees. You can see a reasonably good distance and run as fast as you want.

# Is your home safe because it's white on the map? The 'often-overlooked trap' of hazard maps

[Button: 4 ]

2026年8月11日 08:29

Hello, I'm Nana, a PR representative for Bousai Komachi Co., Ltd., and an active high school student disaster prevention advisor.

Thank you for all your hard work every day with your job, housework, part-time work, and your daily life protecting yourself and your precious family.

Today, I would like to talk about an 'often-overlooked trap' in hazard maps, which I want those of you who have opened your home's hazard map and feel completely at ease thinking, 'My area isn't colored (it's white), so I'm definitely safe from floods and landslides!' to know about.

When your home is in a 'white area' that isn't colored on the municipal hazard map, you feel as if you are protected by an invincible barrier, don't you?

However, over-relying on that 'whiteness' and assuming that 'my home is safe, so there's no need to evacuate' is actually the biggest trap that puts your life at risk during a disaster.

Пантеон

Пантеон (собств. Пантейон) – в древности храмы, посвященные всем богам. Наибольшей известностью пользуется римский П.; сооруженный в 25 или 27 г. до Р. Хр. Марком Агриппой, на Марсовом поле, близ им же построенных терм. Он был посвящен божествам рода Юлиев, статуи которых, например Марса и Венеры, стояли внутри этого сооружения. После неоднократных повреждений, причиненных пожарами и ударами молнии, П. был реставрирован сперва ими. Домицианом и Адрианом, затем. в 202 г. по Р. Хр., Септимием Севером и его сыновьями. Об этой последней реставрации свидетельствует надпись над портиком храма, помещенная под надписью, высеченной Агриппой. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
